experiment: Three scale-fitting objectives for 1-bit experts at IDENTICAL byte cost: plain mean|W|; pooled activation moments; per-EXPERT activation moments accumulated by routed expert id.
RESULT_the_diagnosis_was_correct: Per-expert calibration beats BOTH the uncalibrated baseline and the pooled version: ppl -7.1% at g128 (12.292 -> 11.414) and -10.3% at g64 (12.268 -> 11.005), while pooled was WORSE than uncalibrated (+1.9%, +1.0%). The predicted cause of the pooled failure -- a statistic shared across all 64 experts weighting a parameter fitted per expert -- is confirmed by fixing exactly that and recovering the win. Activation-awareness works here; POOLING was the defect.
FALSIFIES_MY_OWN_COSINE_HYPOTHESIS_AS_A_: Per-expert calibration LOWERS weight-space cosine while IMPROVING perplexity: 0.7995 -> 0.7847 with ppl 12.292 -> 11.414 at g128, and 0.8013 -> 0.7849 with ppl 12.268 -> 11.005 at g64. Cosine and capability move in OPPOSITE directions. That is expected in hindsight -- an activation-weighted fit deliberately trades weight-space fidelity for function-space fidelity -- but it kills any use of cosine as a monotone proxy for representation QUALITY. It survives only as a coarse PASS/FAIL screen across classes, which is a much weaker claim than the one I recorded, and it is the weight-space-proxy trap this project has hit before.
STILL_NOWHERE_NEAR_THE_GATE: Best per-expert arm is ppl 11.005 against a gate of 3.617 and a bf16 reference of 2.894, with median 4-gram 0.9032 against 0.0538. A 10% improvement on a number that must fall by 3.8x is real evidence about mechanism and not progress toward the target.
CAVEATS: 1024 calibration tokens; per-expert counts are therefore thin for rarely-routed experts (64 experts, top-6, so each expert sees roughly 9.4% of token-slots).
Diagonal E[xx^T] only. No correlation structure, no error feedback, no iterative refit.
ppl is a deterministic single forward pass, so these deltas carry no run-to-run noise, unlike the TPS figures elsewhere in this campaign.
